podcast.title: Business Acumen Issues
podcast.body: Many great British indie labels of the 1980s, such as Factory, Two-Tone, and Rough Trade, were poor at business. This led to significant financial problems, including bankruptcies and severe debt, despite their cultural impact. "This highlights a problem with many of those great British indie labels of the 80s. They were crap at doing business."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Physical Release of "In Rainbows"
podcast.body: Following its successful digital "tip jar" release, Radiohead's "In Rainbows" album was also released in physical form through a series of independent labels. This physical release achieved an additional million sales, demonstrating the continued viability of independent distribution channels. "And when the album was released in a physical form through a series of independent labels, they sold another million copies or so."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Alt Rock Chapter: 15

podcast.title: Rise of Power in Digital Age
podcast.body: The music industry in the digital age saw the number of major record labels shrink to just four, leading to a resurgence of small, nimble independent record companies. These indies could quickly capitalize on new music, bands, or trends, providing global distribution without the need for major label backing. "When small, nimble, independent record companies can quickly capitalize on a song or a band or an album or a scene or a trend, no longer did you have to be on a major label to get global distribution of your music."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Alt Rock Chapter: 15

podcast.title: Role in British Music Innovation (1980s)
podcast.body: Dozens of independent labels emerged in Britain throughout the 1980s, acting as a major catalyst for musical innovation. These labels were "nimble and quick," enabling them to get music into stores and bands on tour far more rapidly than major labels, thereby driving the development of British indie culture. "Another thing that spurred innovation in British music through the 80s were the dozens and dozens and dozens of independent labels that popped up."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Swans' Early Releases and Departure
podcast.body: Swans began their career releasing their first albums, *Filth* and *Cop*, on independent labels. These releases had minimal repercussion and sales. The band would later leave independent labels to sign with a major label following the unexpected popularity of their "Love Will Tear Us Apart" cover. "salen mediante discográficas independientes de las que casi no tuvieron repercusión."

podcast.title: Use of 360 Deals
podcast.body: Independent labels also extensively utilized the "360 deal" model, similar to major labels. This business model involves providing upfront financial support to artists in exchange for a share of various revenue streams, enabling both parties to potentially survive and thrive in a market with declining record sales. "Indie labels use this model a lot too."
